scope: Controlled VM evaluation of the actual QA observer with Date.now initially selected and performance.now installed before acquisition; no real timer wait or RN runtime is represented.
reproductionRecipe: Evaluate the actual unchanged tests/native/auth-diagnostics.cjs in a fresh Node VM with Date.now returning 1700000000000 and no performance property.
Create the diagnostic with its default reader and request a lock whose callback waits on an externally controlled promise.
Advance the synthetic wall clock by 5500 ms and install performance.now returning 5500 before resolving the lock gate.
Read the recorded acquired wait and final timestamp: both are 0, while the original callback result remains 7. No real timer wait is performed.
interpretation: The observer can silently clamp an origin-changing clock-provider switch. This characterizes a measurement boundary; it does not establish a React Native runtime switch or explain the SDK warning.
applicability: Pinned RN initializes Performance synchronously before timers and AppRegistry. Its main Performance implementation captures its timestamp provider at module evaluation.

A Date-epoch to performance-origin switch would freeze subsequent relative values near startup; a reverse epoch jump would make values huge. Inspect actual trace progression before treating this scenario as applicable.
No production or currently building diagnostic source was changed. No build restart is justified by this controlled example alone.
